- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.53) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap upward forecasts at 1–2% above recent peak.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative (0.27–0.53) and recent price is falling; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment turns sharply negative.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27–0.80), model tends to smooth out extremes; use sentiment-weighted average to preserve momentum in trending periods.
